name: Aldery Priory: the thirty days
summary: Thirty days alone in a cottage in the Ignatian manner, silent through the mornings, meeting a director each day. For people with an existing prayer life.
description:
Aldery has four cottages in a strip of oak wood above the river and two directors who have accompanied the long retreat for a combined forty years. We offer the thirty days twice a year.

You are alone. Your cottage has a bed, a chair, a table, a stove, and a window onto the wood. You set your own day. We suggest five periods of prayer and a review after each, in the way the Exercises are usually given, but how you distribute them and what you do with the hours between is yours to decide. Most people walk. The hill behind the wood is steep and the paths are long, and by the second week people are walking a great deal.

Silence is kept from Compline until after the midday meal, every day of the thirty. The afternoons are not silent: you meet your director for half an hour, and you may speak with the sisters in the garden, use the telephone in the hall, or talk with whoever is chopping wood. Many people find they use the afternoons for one conversation and otherwise keep quiet, but that is a choice and not a rule.

This is demanding. Thirty days of five prayer periods, early rising, and long silent mornings is a great deal to carry, and people who arrive without a settled daily practice tend to struggle in the first week rather than deepen. We ask that you have done at least one directed retreat of eight days and have a regular practice of prayer or meditation now. We talk this through by telephone before confirming.
practical: Thirty days, offered in February and September. £1,650 including all meals and direction; some bursary help is available, ask. Four cottages, so four people at a time, who will not see each other. Wood stove, cold water in the cottage, shared bathroom in the lodge. Bring boots, warm clothes, a torch, and whatever you pray with. Nearest station Hereford; we collect. Phones may be used in the hall in the afternoons; there is no signal in the cottages and no internet.
